text: In David Albert's account of the arrow of time, what is the 'Past Hypothesis' and what explanatory work does it do?
choices: The claim that the fundamental dynamical laws are themselves time-asymmetric, building a direction directly into physics
The postulate that the universe began in a state of extremely low entropy, which — combined with the dynamical laws and the Statistical Postulate — explains why entropy increases toward the future
The proposal that our present low-entropy universe is a spontaneous thermal fluctuation out of an equilibrium 'heat death' state
The thesis that past events are overdetermined by their many future traces, which grounds the psychological arrow
explanation: Albert's Past Hypothesis is the postulate of a very low-entropy initial state, added to the time-symmetric dynamics and the Statistical Postulate to explain the thermodynamic arrow. Option 0 is false — the laws are time-symmetric, which is precisely why an extra postulate is needed; option 2 is Boltzmann's fluctuation proposal (which invites the Boltzmann Brain reductio); and option 3 is Lewis's asymmetry of overdetermination.
